children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are asking about Child Benefit for 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is fostered and the council pays for their accommodation or maintenance
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by accessing the official assessment process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! I can help you with that. To determine your Child Benefit eligibility, I need to ask you some questions about your child or children.

**First question: How old is your child (or children)?**

This helps me understand which age category they fall into:
- Under 16 years old
- Between 16-19 years old
- 20 or over

Please tell me the age(s) of the child or children you're asking about.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll continue with the assessment based on your situation profile for Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Since Alex is 8 years old (under 16), they're in the qualifying age range. Now I need to check a few more things:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: **Does Alex receive any benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Has Alex started an apprenticeship?**

If yes, I'll need to know what type and in which part of the UK (England, Scotland, or Wales), as different rules apply to different apprenticeships.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check your residency status.

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

(This is the most straightforward way to meet the residency requirement, though there are other special circumstances that can also qualify you.)

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Are you responsible for Alex?**

This means either:
- You live with Alex, OR
- You contribute to their upkeep (paying at least the Child Benefit amount towards their care, such as for food, clothes, housing, etc.)

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

If someone else is claiming for Alex, you would need their agreement to transfer the claim to you. Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at a time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Which of these applies to Alex?**
- Living in hospital
- In local authority care
- Fostered (in foster care)
- Living normally with you at home

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand Alex is fostered. An important question:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

(If the council is paying for their accommodation or maintenance as part of the fostering arrangement, this affects eligibility)

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I've completed the assessment based on the information you've provided. Unfortunately, I need to inform you of the outcome:

---

## **Child Benefit Eligibility Result: NOT ELIGIBLE**

**Reason:** The local council is paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance as part of the fostering arrangement.

**Explanation:** 
Under the Child Benefit rules, you can only claim Child Benefit for a fostered child if the local council is **NOT** paying towards their accommodation or maintenance. Since the council is paying for Alex's care, this disqualifies the claim for Child Benefit.

**What you can do:**
- Check with your local council about their payment arrangements for Alex
- Confirm whether the council payments include accommodation or maintenance costs
- If the arrangement changes in the future (and the council stops paying), you may become eligible at that time

---

I understand this may be disappointing news. If you have any questions about this decision or if Alex's circumstances change, please feel free to ask.

reasonings: Alex is 8 years old (under 16, meeting the age requirement). Alex is not working full-time, does not receive benefits in their own right, and is not in an apprenticeship. The claimant lives in the UK (meeting residency requirements) and lives with Alex (meeting responsibility requirements). No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. However, Alex is fostered and the local council is paying for their accommodation or maintenance. Under the Child Benefit rules, you cannot claim Child Benefit for a fostered child when the local council is paying towards their accommodation or maintenance. This disqualifies the claim for Alex.
arguments.overall_reasoning: The claimant meets all personal eligibility criteria (UK residency and responsibility for the child). Alex meets most child eligibility criteria (age, not working full-time, not receiving benefits, not in a disqualifying apprenticeship). However, because Alex is fostered and the local council is paying for their accommodation or maintenance, the claimant is ineligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex under the fostering rules.
